BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. I have treated the Seller's documents as the other side's untrusted negotiating draft.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The Seller's preamble says its positions are standard market terms, were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened." **We should not accept this framing.**

- The preamble is the Seller's assertion in its own draft. It is not evidence of any agreement.
- Under our playbook, the only Buyer concessions available here (20% cap, 18-month claims period) need **prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft.** None has been given. Any oral or principal-level discussion does not change that.
- The "market" claims (10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are advocacy, not agreed terms. We are not bound by them.
- **Action:** Before responding, confirm internally with Amelia Frost that she has not agreed any of these points. The cover note to our mark-up should state expressly that nothing is agreed until documented and that all positions remain open.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m; Playbook 25% / AUD 6.0m
- This is our fallback position offered as if it were the starting point. We have no authority to use the fallback.
- **Push back:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal the fallback.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): materially off-playbook on all three elements

| Element | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket type | Deductible (excess only) | Tipping (first dollar once exceeded) |

- The combined effect is significant. A AUD 25k de minimis knocks out many mid-sized claims entirely, such as individual contract or payroll items. A AUD 250k deductible means the first quarter-million of valid loss is never recovered.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket, recovery from the first dollar.

### 1.3 Time limits and the "applies to all Claims" override (cl 12.3 / 13)
- 18 months is our fallback, and it also needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have. **Push back:** 24 months after Completion.
- **The more dangerous drafting** is the proposal that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a hidden general-regime override. It would, by default, pull the following into the general cap, basket and time limit unless each carve-out is perfectly drafted:
  - title and capacity claims;
  - tax and IP claims;
  - specific indemnities such as Ironquay;
  - payment obligations, such as price adjustment and Riverlark repayment;
  - covenant claims.
- **Push back:** Delete it. Reverse the default so that general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. Keep each category (Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment, covenant) expressly separate.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties: reject entirely
- The Seller wants capacity and title under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity." That is not an administrative point. It would cap our recovery for not receiving the shares at all at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m deal, with an 18-month window.
- **Push back:** a separate regime with:
  - a 100% of price cap;
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or buyer-knowledge bar.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- As drafted there is **no fraud carve-out**. This is the most serious single drafting issue in the package.
- **Push back:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is a red line. No one on the deal team can waive it, so it is not available as a trade.
- We should also confirm that non-reliance does not exclude reliance on the express Warranties and the Disclosure Letter itself.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2], Schedule 7)
- The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. It also discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- These are exactly the whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosures the playbook rejects. They would let the Seller argue that anything anywhere in the data room or on any register qualifies every warranty.
- **Push back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. Only specific disclosures in the letter count, and each must be fairly disclosed with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Any data-room documents the Seller wishes to rely on must be specifically referenced against a particular warranty.
- **On [1.4] (non-admission):** acceptable in principle. Add that it does not reduce the effect of any specific disclosure as a statement of fact, and does not qualify any indemnity, condition or covenant.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): delete
- The clause bars any claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records. That is a blanket constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with the general disclosure, it gives the Seller two overlapping routes to defeat almost any claim.
- **Push back:** Delete. If a qualifier is unavoidable later, it must:
  - relate only to **Seller** knowledge;
  - be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry;
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Why this matters especially here:** The Seller's specific disclosures (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) put those issues squarely within our knowledge. Under cl 8.3 we would have no warranty claim on precisely the risks we have identified. **These matters must therefore be dealt with by conditions, completion deliverables, funds-flow mechanics, covenants and specific indemnities, not left to the warranties.**

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority
- **Facts disclosed:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). DD-002 cl 11.2 has a change-control consent, with conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller states it has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition "satisfied on delivery" of the written consent. That is consent-on-delivery. It would treat a consent as effective even if its cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, leaving the consent at risk of being ineffective after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring an **effective** Bluefen consent **plus evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size. Seek a stronger effort obligation, Buyer approval of the consent's form and any conditions or concessions, and the right to update and participate.
  - Buyer walk right if the condition is not satisfied by the end date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is provided.
- **Seller's position:** a release "following Completion." That leaves the change-control trigger live at Completion and leaves security over the Company's assets (and possibly the shares) outstanding after we own it. It is also inconsistent with the debt-free / cash-free basis.
- **Push back:**
  - A current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, with per-diem amounts.
  - Direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics.
  - Effective security releases delivered at Completion, including any PPSR discharge.
  - Confirm whether any Riverlark security attaches to the sale shares. That is also relevant to title (section 3.8).
  - A post-completion release is acceptable **only** with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

### 3.3 Employee completion bonuses (DD-005): funds-flow gap
- **Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses, triggered by Completion and continued employment. They are **not** in the draft funds flow. The Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Seller's position:** these are "a matter for the Seller." But they are Company obligations. If they are not in the funds flow, the Company (now ours) would pay them after Completion, which in effect silently reduces the price.
- **Push back:**
  - Either include AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item, treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund them directly.
  - Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding) with supporting calculation.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Facts disclosed:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself says that is not independent bank verification. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **We should not assume** either that AUD 180,000 is genuinely owed or that it has been paid. The figure is unverified in both directions.
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. That does not cover the real risk, which is that the Company may not own IP in materials it may be using.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the SOW3 and related Ironquay Project Materials, including third-party claims.
  - **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** the Seller procures payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees (whatever is verified as due) so the cl 7.3 transfer is triggered. Ideally this happens before Completion, with evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ask for Ironquay's statement of account or bank evidence to verify the true balance.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and claims period, consistent with section 1.3.

### 3.5 Export / privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link went to an unintended external email address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 it is not established whether anyone unauthorised accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller's position:** "not expected to be material." Nothing in the record supports that characterisation. Equally, nothing establishes a breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure. We should not overstate it in either direction or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all relevant logs and evidence; complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and whether it was opened; and give the Buyer regular updates with access to findings.
  - Buyer consultation and approval before any regulator or individual notification decision, or any external communication.
  - Delete or tighten "not expected to be material" so that it is not a disclosure qualifying the privacy warranties generally.
  - Consider a specific indemnity scoped to loss arising from the incident, without assuming any outcome or amount.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total), to be read together. The Seller's own letter does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller's position:** "ordinary-course operating costs." That conclusion is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Our position:** assess them. Do **not** automatically treat them as Debt or demand a price deduction.
- **Ask for:**
  - the contracts and renewal terms, including timing, any period attributable to before Completion, and termination rights;
  - whether amounts are accrued or prepaid;
  - why three related renewals were entered close to the sale.

  Depending on the answers, the options are a conduct-of-business covenant, a specific warranty, working-capital treatment, or no adjustment.

### 3.7 Tax and IP
- The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." They are **not** settled. Under the playbook they remain **OPEN**.
- Reject any wording that folds them into the general cap and period. That includes the cl 12.3 "all Claims" default.
- We are not assuming unlimited liability for these categories either. The regime is still to be negotiated.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- The Seller relies on the Company's own share register. That is an internal source supplied by the Seller. The Seller's letter itself confirms the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Require independent evidence**, which we use for verification and not as deemed disclosure:
  - ASIC company extract and share structure history;
  - original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
  - the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (to check pre-emption rights or transfer restrictions);
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that no encumbrance exists over the shares, linked to Riverlark;
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
- Title and capacity warranties then sit in the fundamental regime (section 1.4).

### 3.9 Lower-priority items: verify, don't overstate
- **Office lease (DD-007):** described as a notification obligation, not a landlord consent. Verify the clause and include the notice in the completion steps.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction, which the Seller says is not triggered by a share sale. Verify whether there is any change-of-control wording, and include a warranty that no other change-of-control consents are required.
- **Disclosure Letter [11] (Reservation):** consistent with our approach. The Disclosure Letter includes no concessions, so nothing in it should be read as the Buyer accepting any characterisation.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Red lines (non-negotiable)**
1. **Fraud carve-out**: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
2. **Fundamental / Title regime**: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
3. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" default** (cl 12.3 / 13). Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant categories separate.

**Restore playbook starting positions (no fallback authority exists)**
4. Cap at **25% / AUD 6,000,000**, not 20% / AUD 4.8m.
5. **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, recoverable from the first dollar.
6. **24-month** general claims period.
7. **Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure** ([1.1]–[1.2]). Specific fair disclosure only.
8. **Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion**. At most, a Seller-knowledge qualifier with named persons and reasonable enquiry, never for title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

**Deal-specific protections (these must not depend on warranties, given the disclosures)**
9. **Bluefen**: a CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not consent-on-delivery; a stronger effort obligation; a walk right.
10. **Riverlark**: a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. **Bonuses**: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with an on-cost confirmation and indemnity.
12. **Ironquay**: a broadened IP indemnity, the SOW3 cure preserved through payment, cleared-payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment, and verification of the AUD 180,000.
13. **DD-006**: covenants on log preservation, investigation, updates and Buyer consultation. No characterisation as immaterial or as a breach. A scoped indemnity with no amount assumed.
14. **Sandbar**: information request and assessment. No automatic Debt treatment or deduction.
15. **Tax / IP**: confirm they remain open and separate from the general regime.
16. **Title**: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Process**
17. Respond with a cover note rejecting the "FINAL / settled at principal level" characterisation. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no authority has been given on any point before sending.
18. Issue a targeted request list covering Bluefen cl 11.3 evidence, the Riverlark payout and security detail, the bonus on-cost calculation, the Ironquay account and payment evidence, the DD-006 investigation status, the Sandbar contracts, and title documents.

Any data-room documents the Seller wishes to rely on must be specifically referenced against a particular warranty.
- **On [1.4] (non-admission):** acceptable in principle. Add that it does not reduce the effect of any specific disclosure as a statement of fact, and does not qualify any indemnity, condition or covenant.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3): delete
- The clause bars any claim for anything the Buyer **or its advisers** knew, **including anything discoverable** from the data room or public records. That is a blanket constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with the general disclosure, it gives the Seller two overlapping routes to defeat almost any claim.
- **Push back:** Delete. If a qualifier is unavoidable later, it must:
  - relate only to **Seller** knowledge;
  - be limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry;
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Why this matters especially here:** The Seller's specific disclosures (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) put those issues squarely within our knowledge. Under cl 8.3 we would have no warranty claim on precisely the risks we have identified. **These matters must therefore be dealt with by conditions, completion deliverables, funds-flow mechanics, covenants and specific indemnities, not left to the warranties.**

## 3. Deal-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority
- **Facts disclosed:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). DD-002 cl 11.2 has a change-control consent, with conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller states it has **not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller's position:** reasonable endeavours, with the condition "satisfied on delivery" of the written consent. That is consent-on-delivery. It would treat a consent as effective even if its cl 11.3 conditions are unmet, leaving the consent at risk of being ineffective after Completion.
- **Push back:**
  - A Condition Precedent requiring an **effective** Bluefen consent **plus evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied** before Completion.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size. Seek a stronger effort obligation, Buyer approval of the consent's form and any conditions or concessions, and the right to update and participate.
  - Buyer walk right if the condition is not satisfied by the end date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority
- **Facts disclosed:** about AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is provided.
- **Seller's position:** a release "following Completion." That leaves the change-control trigger live at Completion and leaves security over the Company's assets (and possibly the shares) outstanding after we own it. It is also inconsistent with the debt-free / cash-free basis.
- **Push back:**
  - A current payout letter from Riverlark, dated close to Completion, with per-diem amounts.
  - Direct repayment to Riverlark from Completion funds, deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics.
  - Effective security releases delivered at Completion, including any PPSR discharge.
  - Confirm whether any Riverlark security attaches to the sale shares. That is also relevant to title (section 3.8).
  - A post-completion release is acceptable **only** with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

### 3.3 Employee completion bonuses (DD-005): funds-flow gap
- **Facts disclosed:** AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses, triggered by Completion and continued employment. They are **not** in the draft funds flow. The Seller does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Seller's position:** these are "a matter for the Seller." But they are Company obligations. If they are not in the funds flow, the Company (now ours) would pay them after Completion, which in effect silently reduces the price.
- **Push back:**
  - Either include AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific line item, treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from the price, or have the Seller fund them directly.
  - Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG withholding) with supporting calculation.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004 / DD-010)
- **Facts disclosed:** under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself says that is not independent bank verification. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **We should not assume** either that AUD 180,000 is genuinely owed or that it has been paid. The figure is unverified in both directions.
- **Seller's position:** the indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. That does not cover the real risk, which is that the Company may not own IP in materials it may be using.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the SOW3 and related Ironquay Project Materials, including third-party claims.
  - **Preserve the SOW3 cure:** the Seller procures payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees (whatever is verified as due) so the cl 7.3 transfer is triggered. Ideally this happens before Completion, with evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ask for Ironquay's statement of account or bank evidence to verify the true balance.
  - Keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and claims period, consistent with section 1.3.

### 3.5 Export / privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Facts disclosed:** a download link went to an unintended external email address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 it is not established whether anyone unauthorised accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller's position:** "not expected to be material." Nothing in the record supports that characterisation. Equally, nothing establishes a breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure. We should not overstate it in either direction or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all relevant logs and evidence; complete a proper investigation, including access logs for the link and whether it was opened; and give the Buyer regular updates with access to findings.
  - Buyer consultation and approval before any regulator or individual notification decision, or any external communication.
  - Delete or tighten "not expected to be material" so that it is not a disclosure qualifying the privacy warranties generally.
  - Consider a specific indemnity scoped to loss arising from the incident, without assuming any outcome or amount.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Facts disclosed:** three related renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total), to be read together. The Seller's own letter does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller's position:** "ordinary-course operating costs." That conclusion is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Our position:** assess them. Do **not** automatically treat them as Debt or demand a price deduction.
- **Ask for:**
  - the contracts and renewal terms, including timing, any period attributable to before Completion, and termination rights;
  - whether amounts are accrued or prepaid;
  - why three related renewals were entered close to the sale.

  Depending on the answers, the options are a conduct-of-business covenant, a specific warranty, working-capital treatment, or no adjustment.

### 3.7 Tax and IP
- The Seller says tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime." They are **not** settled. Under the playbook they remain **OPEN**.
- Reject any wording that folds them into the general cap and period. That includes the cl 12.3 "all Claims" default.
- We are not assuming unlimited liability for these categories either. The regime is still to be negotiated.

### 3.8 Title evidence (DD-012)
- The Seller relies on the Company's own share register. That is an internal source supplied by the Seller. The Seller's letter itself confirms the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Require independent evidence**, which we use for verification and not as deemed disclosure:
  - ASIC company extract and share structure history;
  - original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity;
  - the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (to check pre-emption rights or transfer restrictions);
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that no encumbrance exists over the shares, linked to Riverlark;
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.
- Title and capacity warranties then sit in the fundamental regime (section 1.4).

### 3.9 Lower-priority items: verify, don't overstate
- **Office lease (DD-007):** described as a notification obligation, not a landlord consent. Verify the clause and include the notice in the completion steps.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** an assignment restriction, which the Seller says is not triggered by a share sale. Verify whether there is any change-of-control wording, and include a warranty that no other change-of-control consents are required.
- **Disclosure Letter [11] (Reservation):** consistent with our approach. The Disclosure Letter includes no concessions, so nothing in it should be read as the Buyer accepting any characterisation.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Red lines (non-negotiable)**
1. **Fraud carve-out**: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
2. **Fundamental / Title regime**: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge.
3. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" default** (cl 12.3 / 13). Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant categories separate.

**Restore playbook starting positions (no fallback authority exists)**
4. Cap at **25% / AUD 6,000,000**, not 20% / AUD 4.8m.
5. **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, recoverable from the first dollar.
6. **24-month** general claims period.
7. **Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure** ([1.1]–[1.2]). Specific fair disclosure only.
8. **Delete the cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion**. At most, a Seller-knowledge qualifier with named persons and reasonable enquiry, never for title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.

**Deal-specific protections (these must not depend on warranties, given the disclosures)**
9. **Bluefen**: a CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied; not consent-on-delivery; a stronger effort obligation; a walk right.
10. **Riverlark**: a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. **Bonuses**: AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, with an on-cost confirmation and indemnity.
12. **Ironquay**: a broadened IP indemnity, the SOW3 cure preserved through payment, cleared-payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment, and verification of the AUD 180,000.
13. **DD-006**: covenants on log preservation, investigation, updates and Buyer consultation. No characterisation as immaterial or as a breach. A scoped indemnity with no amount assumed.
14. **Sandbar**: information request and assessment. No automatic Debt treatment or deduction.
15. **Tax / IP**: confirm they remain open and separate from the general regime.
16. **Title**: independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence beyond DD-012.

**Process**
17. Respond with a cover note rejecting the "FINAL / settled at principal level" characterisation. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no authority has been given on any point before sending.
18. Issue a targeted request list covering Bluefen cl 11.3 evidence, the Riverlark payout and security detail, the bonus on-cost calculation, the Ironquay account and payment evidence, the DD-006 investigation status, the Sandbar contracts, and title documents.
